html:
SMTO-CFG-0067 — Saved Agent settings are in a format this SMTO can't read

GUID: 4effaa48-f22b-4817-bab2-5667a27223ff
Slug: policy-schema-unsupported
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO found saved choices about how the Agent works, or which skills and tools it may use, in a format it doesn't know. It stopped the action instead of guessing, and left those choices unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you recently went back to an older SMTO, or restored a backup made by a newer one, open Settings › Setup › Server updates and select Check for updates. Only a matching or newer SMTO can safely read choices that a newer version saved.
  2. Wait for running tasks to finish, then select Update server on that page. SMTO restarts to finish the update. The update gives SMTO the ability to read these saved choices without changing them.
  3. If a script or another program sends tasks to SMTO for you, ask the person who set it up to check the skill and behavior choices it sends. That program may be sending choices in a format this SMTO doesn't accept.
  4. Before repeating the action, open the conversation and check whether the task already started, so you don't run it twice. The failed step may have been part of a larger action, so check before trying again.

What success looks like

  • The conversation opens or the task starts without this message, and the skills and tools listed for it are the ones you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and say which SMTO version you use and whether you restored a backup. Don't hand-edit or delete the saved choices; an unknown format can't be safely converted by hand.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A saved or submitted AgentBehaviorPolicy or AgentCapabilityPolicy has a schema_version other than the integer 1, so the runtime refused to load it.

What this means

  • Behavior or capability policy schema_version is not exactly integer 1. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Behavior or capability policy schema_version is not exactly integer 1.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact stored version type/value and preserve policy data before any supported migration.

How to fix it

  • Find where the snapshot came from (task submission, the conversation's capability_policy_json, the global capability policy, or an imported backup) and check its schema_version. Run a Server version that supports that version instead of editing the data, or fix the integration so it sends schema_version 1; keep the original record unchanged.
  • Use a compatible runtime and its supported migration path. Preserve the original policy data before migration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A compatible version-1 policy validates without silently changing its authority.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
